final.summary: The ETP stopped for about three hours in the afternoon and the tank level rose while outfall pH stayed near neutral, showing the water was held and no untreated water reached the outfall then. Later that evening power stayed below the level required for the inflow while the inflow stayed normal, and the power feed was not a replay. A human must judge whether aeration was cut or the power meter was wrong.

key_evidence.why: Tank rose from 0.41 to 0.73 while ETP was at standby, showing water was held.
Tank balance within tolerance with unaccounted -4.0 m3, showing no bypass loss during stop.
Power at ~4.0 kW confirms ETP stopped as claimed.
Outfall pH stayed near 7.74, showing no raw wastewater reached outfall during stop.
Power was below expected band for entire stretch with normal inflow, showing aeration was reduced.
Inflow stayed normal, so low power is not explained by low load.
No identical stretch, so low power feed is not a replay.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: Outfall flow missing 2026-10-13 11:00 to 22:20, so ETP and boundary balances cannot be computed for that stretch.
No lab BOD result and no power meter photo covers the low-power stretch, so aeration cut cannot be separated from power meter error.
Factory logbook and maintenance record are claims, not facts; maintenance record received before the work date.
Conductivity and pH show where water went, not whether aeration ran.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
